items.title: A finite graded module over a graded polynomial algebra that is flat over a local ring is finitely presented
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a finite graded module over a graded polynomial algebra over a local ring is finitely presented as soon as it is flat over the base ring. The proof chooses homogeneous generators, writes down the resulting presentation by free graded modules, examines it degree by degree, and observes that each graded piece of the module is finite flat, hence free, over the local ring, which makes each graded piece of the kernel finite flat and therefore free. The kernel is then generated by finitely many homogeneous elements: after tensoring the degreewise sequences with the residue field, Noetherianity of the graded polynomial algebra over the residue field provides finitely many homogeneous elements whose images generate, and Nakayama's lemma upgrades that to generation over the base ring.
